current_row.boundary_rationale: The span's front seam, at Lam.3.60/Lam.3.61, rests on the acrostic letter change from resh to shin, and no accompanying voice, addressee or topic shift falls at either verse; the direct address to YHWH about the enemies' hostility continues across that seam without a content break, disclosed here as part of this span's own confidence assessment. The shin and tav triplets (3:61-63, 3:64-66) close the whole triple acrostic, reporting the enemies' plotting under direct address to YHWH through 3:61-3:63, the shin triplet's one true imperative anchored at הַבִּ֔יטָה (oshb:Lam.3.63, byte tier) amid its closing report clauses, before turning, in the tav triplet, to three verse-initial second-masculine-singular prefix-conjugation verbs of prospective retribution against them, each verse-initial in the same construction (sweep: 3 verses): תָּשִׁ֨יב לָהֶ֥ם גְּמ֛וּל יְהוָ֖ה כְּמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יְדֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Lam.3.64, byte tier), תִּתֵּ֤ן לָהֶם֙ מְגִנַּת לֵ֔ב תַּאֲלָֽתְךָ֖ לָהֶֽם (oshb:Lam.3.65, byte tier) and תִּרְדֹּ֤ף בְּאַף֙ וְתַשְׁמִידֵ֔ם מִתַּ֖חַת שְׁמֵ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Lam.3.66, byte tier); the WEB witness renders the opening verb “You will pay them back, Yahweh, according to the work of their hands.” (web:Lam.3.64) and the closing verb, at the poem's own final verse, “You will pursue them in anger, and destroy them from under the heavens of Yahweh.” (web:Lam.3.66). The closing shift from report to prospective retribution, beginning at Lam.3.64, stands as this span's own interior texture; the front boundary against extending back into the qof/resh material is carried instead by the resh-to-shin letter change at Lam.3.60/Lam.3.61. The same closing shift is an operative-category deviation from a plain unit_type label, disclosed here rather than left silent.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The stanza sequence opens the chapter with אֵיכָה֙ יוּעַ֣ם זָהָ֔ב (oshb:Lam.4.1, byte tier), rendered by the WEB witness “How the gold has become dim!” (web:Lam.4.1); its opening word אֵיכָה֙ also opens the poems at Lam.1.1 and Lam.2.1 (accent_stripped tier; sweep: 4 hits book-wide, verse-initial in three of them). Two verses of tarnished-treasure imagery, the gold and the sons of Zion counted as pitchers, give way to the narrator's indictment that “the daughter of my people has become cruel” (web:Lam.4.3), her cruelty toward her young set against nursing jackals — the verse's own doubled ketiv/qere pair disclosed here: unpointed ketiv תנין against pointed qere תַּנִּים֙ for the jackals themselves, and unpointed ketiv כי ענים against pointed qere כַּיְעֵנִ֖ים for the ostrich comparison (oshb:Lam.4.3, both notes single-witness apparatus), the plural nursing-jackals wording here following the qere rather than the singular ketiv — then pressed further by the Sodom comparison that closes the group: “the iniquity of the daughter of my people is greater than the sin of Sodom” (web:Lam.4.6). The stanzas run aleph, bet, gimel, dalet, he and vav, positions one through six of the reversed pe-before-ayin sequence that governs this chapter. The span's back seam, at Lam.4.6/Lam.4.7, turns on the shift from the Sodom-comparison indictment to the nobles' description beginning at Lam.4.7, weighed against the bat-ami phrase's own recurrence at Lam.4.10, disclosed in device_notes as a pull toward continuity across this seam.

The close verse turns the same address back toward Zion and Edom together: בַּת צִיּ֔וֹן stands in 4:22 (oshb:Lam.4.22, byte tier), and פָּקַ֤ד עֲוֺנֵךְ֙ בַּת אֱד֔וֹם closes the same verse (oshb:Lam.4.22, byte tier) — “He will visit your iniquity, daughter of Edom.” (web:Lam.4.22). The stanzas run shin and tav, the closing two letters of the chapter's acrostic.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The fifth poem opens without an acrostic but with a three-imperative chain: זְכֹ֤ר יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Lam.5.1, byte tier) is followed in the same verse by a ketiv-qere pair, הביט הַבִּ֖יטָה (oshb:Lam.5.1, byte tier; the inventory's own K/Q note here), both readings meaning look or regard, and then by a third imperative carrying its own vav prefix, וּרְאֵ֥ה (oshb:Lam.5.1, byte tier); the full verse, זְכֹ֤ר יְהוָה֙ מֶֽה הָ֣יָה לָ֔נוּ הביט הַבִּ֖יטָה וּרְאֵ֥ה אֶת חֶרְפָּתֵֽנוּ (oshb:Lam.5.1, byte tier), reads “Remember, Yahweh, what has come on us. Look, and see our reproach.” (web:Lam.5.1). As a petition imperative to the divine name, the remember-form stands in 2 verses, here and at web:Lam.3.19 (skeleton tier), the third member of its 3-verse bare-token census being the negated third-person perfect at web:Lam.2.1; the look-form stands in 2 verses as a bare token and in 4 under the single-letter prefix test, at web:Lam.1.11, web:Lam.2.20, web:Lam.3.63 and web:Lam.5.1 (skeleton tier at both digits). The communal voice then catalogs loss across 5:2-5:10 without a further direct address to YHWH: inheritance surrendered, “We are orphans and fatherless. Our mothers are as widows.” (web:Lam.5.3), water and wood bought at a price, foreign servitude, inherited guilt, and at the group's own close, עוֹרֵ֨נוּ֙ כְּתַנּ֣וּר נִכְמָ֔רוּ מִפְּנֵ֖י זַלְעֲפ֥וֹת רָעָֽב (oshb:Lam.5.10, byte tier), “Our skin is black like an oven, because of the burning heat of famine.” (web:Lam.5.10) — the catalogue's 1st-plural form closing before a four-verse gap at Lam.5.11-Lam.5.14 (1st-plural sweep: 0 of those 4 verses), where a run of third-plural verbs on bare plural human-group subjects opens at 5:11.

current_row.boundary_rationale: This group opens on its own texture rather than continuing what precedes it: 5:11 through 5:14 (4 verses) each open with a bare plural human-group noun followed by a third-plural verb — נָשִׁים֙ בְּצִיּ֣וֹן עִנּ֔וּ בְּתֻלֹ֖ת בְּעָרֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Lam.5.11, byte tier), “They ravished the women in Zion, the virgins in the cities of Judah.” (web:Lam.5.11); שָׂרִים֙ (oshb:Lam.5.12, byte tier); בַּחוּרִים֙ (oshb:Lam.5.13, byte tier); and זְקֵנִים֙ (oshb:Lam.5.14, byte tier) — none of the four carrying a 1st-plural form, against the 1st-plural catalogue that runs unbroken through the verse immediately in front of this span, web:Lam.5.10 (1st-plural sweep: 10 of 10 verses, Lam.5.1-Lam.5.10). The catalog continues from economic loss into social and personal violation: “The young men carry millstones.
